title: Service fitness gating and stable autoscaler handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see transient SLO regressions during regional failovers and sudden traffic shifts driven by noisy readiness/liveness signals and aggressive scale-down behavior. Current readiness checks are single-signal, thresholded, and cause rapid instance state flips which trigger the autoscaler to oscillate. During handoffs between regions this results in doubled tail latency and increased error budgets for affected tenants.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight, production-safe 'service fitness' gating layer that consumes multiple health signals, smooths noise, and coordinates an explicit handoff with the autoscaler to prevent thrash while preserving SLOs. This ticket implements the control path and observability needed for rollout and verification.

Design proposal: 1) Composite fitness score: ingest existing signals (latency p95/p99, per-instance 5xx rate, request queue depth, KV cache local hit rate, synthetic-synthetic-liveness) and compute a normalized fitness score in [0.0, 1.0]. 2) Temporal dampening: apply a short EMA plus an outlier filter (Hampel window) to suppress single-sample spikes. Tuning knobs: ema_alpha, outlier_window_ms, min_samples_for_transition. 3) Tiers & state machine: map fitness into three states: Active (>=0.85), Degraded (0.5-0.85), Draining (<0.5). State transitions require a configurable confirmation window. 4) Autoscaler handshake: when an instance transitions to Draining initiate an autoscaler handoff protocol: mark instance as draining, annotate with handoff_token, delay scale-down decisions for handoff_grace_period, and emit handoff start/commit events. Autoscaler will treat handoff_token semantics to avoid immediate scale-in. 5) Circuit-breaker integration: expose a region-level aggregated fitness and if whole-region fitness < 0.4 trigger gradual traffic spill to fallback region with rate-limited steps, not a hard cutover. 6) Synthetic priming: when scaled-up capacity is added, run small synthetic traffic to prime KV caches and mount readiness after synthetic success to minimize cold-start tail.

Observability & SLOs: add metrics: composite_fitness, fitness_state{instance,region}, fitness_ema_alpha, autoscaler_handoff_events, handoff_latency_seconds, synthetic_priming_success. Create a SLO dashboard showing error budget burn with/without handoff and a playbook that correlates handoff events with SLO regressions.

Acceptance criteria: - Composite fitness computed and emitted as metric for all serving nodes. - No scale-in for instances with active handoff_token for at least handoff_grace_period (unit test + e2e). - Controlled failover simulation (chaos run) demonstrates >=30% reduction in p99 tail compared to current baseline for two injected failure modes (probe flapping, regional latency spike). - Circuit-breaker spillover limits traffic to fallback region in five linear steps and exposes metrics for each step. - Runbook and dashboard created with clear alert thresholds and a retrospective checklist.

Rollout plan: 1) Library + metric + unit tests (canary internal cluster) 2) Autoscaler handshake implementation + local simulation (staging) 3) Enable composite fitness read on one non-critical region, monitor for 48h 4) Toggle autoscaler handshake for same region and run synthetic failover test 5) Incrementally enable in production with feature flag and SLO guardrails 6) Full rollout.

Testing plan: - Unit tests for fitness calculation edge cases. - Integration tests between fitness service and autoscaler simulator. - Chaos simulations: (a) intermittent readiness flips, (b) cross-region latency injection. - Load tests to validate priming reduces cold-start p99.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-calibration could keep unhealthy nodes active. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and short confirmation windows; circuit-breaker still will route away at region level. - Risk: added telemetry cardinality. Mitigation: sample at 1m resolution and expose rollup metrics. - Risk: autoscaler compatibility regressions. Mitigation: staged rollout and automated rollback on SLO degradation.

Notes: This approach favors a small, auditable control surface (fitness score + token handshake) rather than replacing the autoscaler. It aims for predictable behavior during orchestrated handoffs and chaotic failures while remaining reversible.
